2026-08-10T03:44:35.8536145Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8536571Z 
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8536937Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8537502Z 
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8537952Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8538543Z 
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8540492Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8543049Z >
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8546176Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8549265Z >
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8550198Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8551137Z 
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8551324Z ### How to Use
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8551570Z 
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8552403Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8553305Z 
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8553701Z ```bash
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8554320Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8555148Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8555841Z ```
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8556072Z 
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8556351Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8556940Z ```bash
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8557541Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8558456Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8559444Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8560302Z ```
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8560515Z 
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8561236Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8562245Z ```bash
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8562861Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8563817Z ```
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8564042Z 
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8564553Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8565339Z ```bash
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8565939Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8566957Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8567755Z ```
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8567972Z 
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8568257Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8568747Z 
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8570512Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8572505Z 
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8572682Z ```bash
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8573152Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8574317Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8575286Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8575626Z 
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8576153Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8577334Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8578268Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8578776Z ```
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8578993Z 
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8579896Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8581006Z 
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8581185Z ```bash
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8581924Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8582946Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8583916Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8584422Z 
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8584890Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8585823Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8586429Z ```
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8586643Z 
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8586864Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8587790Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8588943Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8590125Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8591314Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8592558Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8593192Z 
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8593377Z ### Notes
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8593813Z 
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8594574Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8596295Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8597794Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8599291Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8600731Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8602038Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8603170Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8604137Z </mcp-clis>
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8604560Z <github-context>

2026-08-10T03:44:35.8621095Z relevant top Hacker News stories on technology that can be used today
2026-08-10T03:44:35.8622089Z by large companies. Every weekday, fetch the top 30 stories from the

2026-08-10T03:44:35.8625201Z engineering, cloud infrastructure, AI/ML, developer tooling, or
